title.full: What happens to CPF monies after death

summary.text: CPF monies follow a valid nomination. Without one, the Public Trustee distributes them under the law.

details.heading: If there is a nomination
details.body: The CPF Board pays the monies to nominees who are older than 18. If a nominee is below 18, the Public Trustee holds the money in trust, unless she is a widow.

details.heading: If there is no nomination
details.body: The CPF Board sends the monies to the Public Trustee for distribution under the law.

details.heading: How the money is distributed
details.body: For non-Muslims, the Intestate Succession Act 1967 applies. For Muslim CPF members, the Administration of the Muslim Law Act 1966 applies.

sources.page_title: What happens to the CPF monies of a deceased CPF member?

quotes.text: The CPF monies of a deceased will be distributed according to the nomination they made during their lifetime.
If there is a nomination, the CPF Board will pay the monies directly to the nominees (if they are older than 18 years old).
If the deceased person did not make a valid nomination, the CPF Board will send the deceased's CPF monies to the Public Trustee for distribution, under the law.
The un-nominated CPF monies paid to the Public Trustee will be distributed according to the Intestate Succession Act 1967 for non-Muslims.
